cases.name: Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War
cases.headline: Defense supply-chain exclusion upheld
cases.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
cases.holding: A divided panel denied Anthropic’s petitions challenging its exclusion from the Department’s supply chain under § 4713. The majority rejected the First Amendment retaliation claim, attributing the exclusion to disputed contract terms rather than protected advocacy.
cases.effect: Leaves the challenged exclusion in place for Department procurement and contractors’ work for the Department. It does not impose a blanket ban on contractors’ unrelated commercial dealings with Anthropic.
cases.limits: Federal appellate decision, not a D.C. local law or a ruling on California’s statutes. This is separate from the California § 3252 case; it is not an appeal reversing that judgment. Multistate relevance does not mean every state’s law changed.
cases.reviewStatus: September 25 merits opinion reviewed. Subsequent rehearing, mandate, or Supreme Court developments have not been verified.

cases.name: Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War et al.
cases.headline: Broader Anthropic restrictions held unlawful
cases.court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
cases.law: 10 U.S.C. § 3252; First Amendment; Administrative Procedure Act
cases.holding: The court ruled largely for Anthropic on summary judgment, finding unlawful retaliation and defects in the § 3252 designation and related directives. It found permanent injunctive relief and vacatur appropriate.
cases.effect: Blocks challenged government actions, including the sweeping contractor boycott, subject to the relief’s limits. The government can still lawfully choose other suppliers. The separate § 4713 exclusion must also be considered.
cases.limits: A federal district-court ruling concerning specified government actions, not a change to California state law or a general right to military contracts. Relief excludes some defendants; the decision is not binding precedent for every court.
cases.reviewStatus: August 27 merits ruling reviewed. Any later appeal or stay of the final relief has not been verified; read together with the September 25 D.C. decision.

timeline.text: Summary judgment ruling and final relief entered.

cases.name: X.AI LLC v. Rob Bonta
cases.headline: California training-data law survives initial injunction bid
cases.court: U.S. District Court, Central District of California
cases.reach: California law · covered developers serving Californians
cases.holding: The court denied xAI’s request for a preliminary injunction against AB 2013. On the early record, xAI had not established likely success on its constitutional claims, including compelled speech and trade-secret arguments.
cases.effect: This order did not halt the disclosure law. It is an early procedural outcome, not a final judgment that resolves every constitutional challenge.
cases.limits: Concerns a California statute, including covered developers outside California that make systems available to Californians. It does not extend AB 2013 to every state or create nationwide binding precedent.
cases.reviewStatus: Appeal docketed in the Ninth Circuit as 26-1591. The reviewed public docket records a September 4 reply brief; no later appellate merits ruling was verified.

timeline.text: Reply brief filed in the appeal.
